 Judgment

These two appeals are arising out of judgment and award in ECA.No.243/2014 dated 17.07.2017 on the file of II Addl Sr.Civil Judge & Commissioner for Employees Compensation ('Tribunal' for short), Kalaburagi, whereby the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioners granting compensation in a sum of Rs.10,59,000/- with interest at 12% p.a. and directed the respondent to pay the same.

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioners that they are the wife, children and father of the deceased Sathishkumar Kulkarni.
He was working as a lineman with respondent.
On 03.02.2012, at about 9.55 p.m, after completion of work, at Andur village, he was returning home on motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 34/E-8644 on Nawbad-Bidar main road.
Near Air Force officers residential area, when he applied brake to avoid newly constructed speed breaker, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died and hence the petition.
5. Respondent appeared and filed objections admitting that deceased was an employee of respondent/corporation, but denied that his death was arising out of and during the course of his employment.
On his death all the benefits payable as a permanent employee have been given including compensatory job to petitioner No.1 and prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. In support of petitioners claim, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW-1 and Ex.P1 to 15 are marked.
8. Respondent has not led any oral and documentary evidence.
9. Vide impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has allowed the petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.10,59,000/- with interest at 12% p.a. and directed the respondent to pay the same.

10. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, respondent has filed appeal contending that the impugned judgment and award is without authority and jurisdiction and as such liable to be set aside.
11. Deceased Sathishkumar Kulkarni was working as Assistant lineman.
He was absorbed in the said post on regular basis.
He was not a temporary employee.
He was in the permanent post.

Consequently, he was not falling within the definition of employee under the Employees'
Compensation Act (for short 'the Act').
Therefore, Tribunal invoking the provisions under the said Act itself is without jurisdiction and as such liable to be set aside.
12. Respondent has further contended that deceased Sathishkumar Kulkarni was a regular employee of respondent/corporation and service regulations framed by the corporation is applicable.
Any benefits for the death of employee is required to be granted or allowed is only under the Karnataka Electricity Board Employees' Service Regulations.

entities.text: Karnataka Electricity Board Employees' Service Regulations
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: When there are specific provisions for providing death benefits to the deceased employee, the provisions under the Act cannot be made applicable and it gets excluded.
The Tribunal has failed to appreciate these aspects and thereby fell into error.
The same is without jurisdiction and liable to be set aside.
Since the deceased was regular employee of respondent/corporation, after his death all the benefits payable under the Service Regulations have been given to the family members of the deceased.
Petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased has been provided with appointment on compassionate ground.
She is presently working with the Corporation and drawing salary in the pay scale of Rs.8480-20600.
After getting all the benefits, petitioner have made a misleading claim at the cost of public money.

sentences.text: The death of deceased was nothing to do with his employment.
Such being the case, it cannot be said that his death was arising out of and during the course of employment.
13. Alternatively it is submitted that at the time of his death, deceased was aged 42 years.

Therefore,
multiplication factor considered by the Tribunal is incorrect.

14. Vide this Court order dated 10.06.2020, the appeal is admitted on the following substantial questions of law:
"a) Whether this appeal is maintainable under the provisions of Employees Compensation Act, 1923?
b) Whether the Commissioner has passed an order in accordance with Employees Compensation Act, 1923 in granting compensation?"

15. On the other hand petitioners have challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that the Tribunal has erred in not taking the net salary at Rs.11,500/- and considering only 50% of the same for calculating the compensation.
The Tribunal has erred in deducting Rs.3,096/- towards LIC, professional tax, UF and DRP, FBF, PC out of gross salary of Rs.14,549/-.
It ought to have deducted only Rs.150/- towards professional tax and prays to allow the appeal.

16. Heard arguments and perused the record.
17.

Thus, respondent/employer has challenged the impugned judgment and award mainly on the ground that deceased was a permanent employee and as such the provisions of Karnataka Electricity Board Employees' Service Regulations are applicable to him and in fact on his death all the death benefits which were due have been paid to his family members and petitioner No.1, the wife of deceased is also given appointment on compassionate grounds and therefore the provisions of the Act are not applicable.

entities.text: Karnataka Electricity Board Employees' Service Regulations
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Without appreciating this fact, the Tribunal has mechanically allowed the claim petition granting compensation.
18. On the other hand petitioners have challenged the impugned judgment and award on quantum and seeking enhancement.
19. It is not in dispute that deceased Sathishkumar Kulkarni was a permanent employee of respondent/corporation.

Consequently the provisions of Karnataka Electricity Board Employees'
Service Regulations are applicable to him.

Karnataka Electricity Board Employees'
Service Regulations
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: During the course of her cross-examination petitioner No.1 who is examined as PW-1 has admitted that on the death of her husband, all the benefits due have been paid and she is also appointed on compassionate grounds and presently she is working in the respondent/corporation.

Such being the case, the provisions of the Workmen Compensation Act (Employees Compensation Act) which is meant for the benefit of temporary employees or to those employees who are not having service benefits and such security is not applicable to the case of the Jyoti And Ors vs Executive Engineer on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50512094/
5 petitioners.

entities.text: Jyoti And Ors vs Executive Engineer on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Without appreciating this aspect, the Tribunal has mechanically allowed the claim petition.
20. Moreover, deceased died in a motor vehicle accident after completion of the work on that day and on while going home.
Such being the case, it cannot be said that his death was arising out of and during the course of employment.
Moreover, when the deceased was not falling under the definition of employee, question of entertaining the petition under the provisions of the Act and granting compensation would not arise.
The very petition itself under the provisions of the Act is not maintainable.
Consequently, the petition itself is liable to be dismissed.
21. For the foregoing reasons the petition filed under Section 3, 10 & 4(i) of the Workman Compensation Act is not maintainable, since the deceased was a permanent employee of respondent/corporation.
Consequently, the Tribunal is not justified in allowing the claim petition and accordingly, the substantial questions of law are answered.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) MFA.No.202312/2017 filed by respondent is allowed.
(ii) MFA.Crob.No.200029/2018 is dismissed.
(iii) Consequently claim petition is dismissed.
(iv) Respondent/employer is permitted to withdraw the amount in deposit (if any).
(v) The registry is directed to send back the trial court records along with the copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
